Question: Christopher Oscar Pena was recognized by an entertainment-industry brand aimed at what?
Thought 1: I need to search Christopher Oscar Pena, find the entertainment-industry brand that recognized him, and then find what that brand is aimed at.
Action 1: Search[Christopher Oscar Pena]
Observation 1: Christopher Oscar Peña is a playwright, screenwriter, actor and educator who resides in New York City. He teaches theater at NYU's Tisch School of Arts[1] and is a member of the Playwrights Unit at Goodman Theatre in Chicago.[1] He also has had work commissioned by Yale Repertory Theatre.[1] Peña co-wrote one episode of the Golden Globe nominated TV series, Jane the Virgin in 2010. He was on the "Future Broadway Power List," by Backstage (magazine) in 2014.[2]. Peña was born in San Jose, California.[3]. His parents emigrated from Honduras.[4].
Thought 2: Christopher Oscar Peña was recognized by "Backstage (magazine)". I need to find what Backstage (magazine) is aimed at.
Action 2: Search[Backstage (magazine)]
Observation 2: Backstage, also previously written as Back Stage, is a global casting platform and entertainment industry publication that connects performers, content creators, and behind-the-scenes professionals with casting directors and production teams across film, television, theater, commercials, and digital media.. Founded in New York City as an industry trade magazine by Allen Zwerdling and Ira Eaker in 1960, the brand now encompasses Backstage.com—which features editorial content and a vetted job listings platform, Backstage magazine, and Call Sheet (formerly Ross Reports)—a directory of talent agents, casting directors, and casting calls.. In the 1990s, Back Stage established the Los Angeles–based Back Stage West, which competed primarily with the longer-established Drama-Logue; in 1998, Drama-Logue was acquired by Back Stage and merged into Back Stage West. In 2008, both versions were merged into a single national edition.. From the 1990s through the early 2010s, Backstage was a sister to fellow entertainment publications Billboard and The Hollywood Reporter, and later Adweek, via Billboard Publications and its corporate successors, such as Nielsen Business Media and Prometheus Global Media.
Thought 3: Backstage (magazine) is a global casting platform and entertainment industry publication that connects performers, content creators, and behind-the-scenes professionals with casting directors and production teams across film, television, theater, commercials, and digital media.
